title: Live events and locks across several app instances
request: With several app instances behind a load balancer, the chat and pipeline streams, the per-draft agent turn lock and the model pause must work when requests land on different instances.
spec: Events as rows with a sequence per draft, the stream woken by LISTEN/NOTIFY and replayed from Last-Event-ID; the per-draft turn lock an advisory lock; the model pause a row with an expiry; tested with two app processes and one worker on one database. Done when a page connected to one instance shows events produced through the other, and two messages to one draft never interleave.
plan: Map what 9.2 already provides on PostgreSQL (numbered event rows, the advisory turn lock, row-locked writes) and what still assumes one process (the stream's poll, the busy check, the model pause in module memory).
Check that reply runs inside the turn lock and that the installed psycopg supports waiting for notifications with a timeout.
Send pg_notify in the transaction that writes each draft event; one listener thread per server process wakes the streams waiting on that draft; keep the 2-second poll as the fallback.
Make 'the agent is still answering' (409) ask the shared turn lock as well as this instance's queued turn.
Move the model pause to a model_pause row with an expiry (migration 0011), keyed by endpoint, model and a hash of the API key.
Test with two server processes and one worker process on one database; gate and reviewer; fix; commit.

decisions.decision: A notice only wakes a stream; the stream still reads the rows and replays from Last-Event-ID.
decisions.why: A missed notice then only delays a stream to its poll, never loses an event.

decisions.decision: The pause key includes a hash of the API key.
decisions.why: A new key must not stay paused by the old key's refusal, and the key itself must never be stored.

decisions.decision: A turn's user message and its answer are written under the turn lock.
decisions.why: That, not the 409 check, is what guarantees two messages never interleave across instances.

change: New dclab_rnd/storage/notify.py (emit and a Listener with subscribe and unsubscribe), dclab_rnd/models/pause.py (a shared pause row with a local fallback), migration 0011; draft events send pg_notify; the stream route waits on the listener; the busy check asks the advisory lock before this instance's own queued turn. tests/test_multi_instance.py starts two server processes and a worker.

findings.defect: Two messages sent at once to the same instance were both accepted.
findings.scenario: Two concurrent POST /api/drafts/{id}/messages after the start turn returned [202, 202] (the second got 409 before); the second task overwrote jobs[key], and the first turn's cleanup then removed the second's entry, so shutdown no longer cancelled it.
findings.cause: The new 'await asyncio.to_thread(answering, ...)' sat between the in-memory jobs check and background(), breaking a check-then-act that used to run in one go on the event loop.
findings.fix: Await the shared-lock probe first, then do the jobs check and background() with no await between them.

findings.defect: A notice could be missed between reading the events and starting to wait.
findings.scenario: The stream reads no events, an event commits after the SELECT's snapshot and before the stream registers its waiter; the wake finds no waiter and the stream sleeps up to 2 s, worse than the old 0.4 s poll, likely during token bursts and for a turn's last event.
findings.cause: The waiter was registered after the read.
findings.fix: The stream subscribes once before its loop, clears its event before each read and waits on it after; it unsubscribes in finally.
findings.test: Covered by the multi-instance stream test.

findings.defect: The listener needed psycopg 3.2 while the requirements allowed 3.1, and failed silently.
findings.scenario: On psycopg 3.1, conn.notifies(timeout=...) raises TypeError right after connecting; the bare except swallowed it and reconnected every 2 s for ever, so LISTEN never worked and nothing was logged.
findings.cause: A version floor below the API used, and an exception swallowed without a word.
findings.fix: Require psycopg 3.2 or later; the listener prints the exception type once, and again after a reconnect.

findings.defect: A stream's limit no longer bounded how long it stayed open.
findings.scenario: A ?wait=1 stream while events keep arriving (a long pipeline, token streaming) stayed open until the events stopped, where it closed after about 1 s before.
findings.cause: Waiting time was counted only on the waiting path, never on the path that read new events.
findings.fix: Elapsed time is measured from a start clock; keep-alives use a separate quiet clock.

findings.defect: The local pause was ignored when the database read succeeded.
findings.scenario: The upsert of a pause fails on a connection blip; the next get() reads the database successfully, finds no row, and a request is sent again to a key the provider refused.
findings.cause: get() returned only the database row when the read worked.
findings.fix: get() returns the later of the local and the shared pause and drops an expired local entry.

findings.defect: No test showed the new cross-instance 409.
findings.scenario: If answering() always returned False every test would still pass: the helper retried on 409 without asserting one, and the lock alone keeps messages from interleaving.
findings.cause: The tests covered the guarantee, not the check.
findings.fix: Add a test that holds the turn lock elsewhere and expects 409.

outcome: Done after one review round: draft events notify every instance, the busy check and turn lock are shared, the model pause is a shared row; a test with two server processes and one worker shows a stream on one instance receiving what the other and the worker produce, and concurrent messages answered one after the other. Left open: a message arriving just as another instance takes the lock waits rather than being refused; the listener needs a direct connection (behind a pooler in transaction mode streams fall back to the poll).
lessons: Adding an await inside a check-then-act on the event loop turns it into a race.
Subscribe before you read, or a notice between the read and the wait is lost.
An exception swallowed in a reconnect loop hides a permanent failure; log its type at least once.
Test the check you added, not only the guarantee another mechanism already provides.
